findings.problem: BatchWorkflow has no typestate enum; lifecycle is encoded as mutable booleans and a string that any caller can mutate to illegal combinations
findings.failure_mode: callers can set is_validated=true and is_sent=true without proper ordering, or set is_sent=true while status=queued, producing unreachable domain states
findings.fix: replace status, is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms with a single BatchState enum where each variant owns its lifecycle data (e.g., BatchState::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }) and mark_sent returns the new state variant

findings.problem: status: String allows any string value including typos, empty strings, and values that do not correspond to valid lifecycle states
findings.failure_mode: a caller can set status to "queued", "QUEUED", "", or "sent" inconsistently with is_sent/is_validated booleans, making state reasoning impossible
findings.fix: replace String with a sealed BatchStatus enum with explicit variants (Queued, Validated, Sent) and implement Display for any serialization needs

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are independent lifecycle booleans that can be set in any combination independent of status
findings.failure_mode: is_validated=true and is_sent=false with status=sent is a reachable but impossible domain state; is_validated=false and is_sent=true bypasses validation entirely
findings.fix: fold both booleans into a single typestate enum that enforces valid transitions and makes invalid combinations unrepresentable

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is a separate field from the lifecycle booleans, so sent_at_epoch_ms can be Some(...) while is_sent=false, or None while is_sent=true
findings.failure_mode: sent_at_epoch_ms is decoupled from the actual sent state, producing inconsistent records where metadata contradicts the boolean lifecycle flags
findings.fix: move sent_at_epoch_ms into the BatchState::Sent variant so it exists only when the batch is in the sent state, making the association enforced by the type system

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive that carries no domain constraints; any string is accepted as a valid batch ID
findings.failure_mode: empty strings, whitespace, duplicate IDs, or malformed identifiers are indistinguishable from valid batch IDs at the type level, enabling bugs that propagate through the system
findings.fix: introduce a newtype BatchId(String or Vec<u8>) with a smart constructor that validates the ID format and returns a typed error on invalid input

findings.problem: raw primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly
findings.failure_mode: no constructor or parse layer exists to validate id, status, or lifecycle fields at the boundary; every caller bypasses domain invariants by instantiating BatchWorkflow fields directly
findings.fix: add a BatchWorkflow::parse or BatchWorkflow::new that takes raw primitives, validates them with fallible smart constructors, and returns Result<BatchWorkflow, ParseError>; make all struct fields private and expose only the validated typestate through the parse layer

residual_risk: strict static review only; no commands executed. All struct fields are public with no typestate enforcement, no smart constructors, no parse boundary, and no typed error taxonomy. A caller can construct any illegal state combination (invalid status strings, contradictory boolean pairs, orphaned epoch timestamps) without any compile-time or runtime guard. The mark_sent function on line 9 performs unchecked string mutation to status without any transition validation.
